stem.en: A model gets a big sum wrong when it writes only the answer, and right when it writes its working first. Which reason fits best?

text.en: It learns while it writes, so each new line is better than the last
It looks each step up in a stored table of worked sums it has kept
Writing the steps changes its settings, so it gets better at sums
Each token gets fixed work, and the written steps stay in the window

explanation.en: A model does the same fixed amount of work for every token, so a whole big sum rarely fits in one token. The written steps go into the context window and are read again, so each step stays small. Using a model changes no setting, and real models keep no table of sums.
